newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO police free Palestinian-American journalist.
newsitem.headline: PLO police free Palestinian-American journalist.

text.p: Palestinian police freed Palestinian-American journalist Daoud Kuttab on Tuesday after holding him without charges for a week.

Kuttab told reporters at his home in Arab East Jerusalem that police did not say why he was being detained but he assumed it had to do with his live broadcasts of Palestinian Legislative Council sessions.
"Nobody told me that directly but that's my assumption," he said. "I went on a hunger strike demanding that they accuse me or release me. They didn't. They had no instructions."
Kuttab, who holds U.S. citizenship, was jailed after obeying a summons by Palestinian police and going to the self-rule enclave of Ramallah in the West Bank last Tuesday.

His brother, attorney Jonathan Kuttab, said it appeared Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's self-rule administration did not like the live transmission of parliament sessions in which legislators complained about government policy.

"These sessions are very open, very democratic and frank and sometimes very critical of the Palestinian Authority," Jonathan Kuttab said on Sunday. He had said his brother was jailed on orders from Arafat.

The United States condemned the Palestinian Authority for the detention and human rights groups described it a part of a "pattern of harassment" against journalists, human rights monitors and other government critics.

"I think I'm more determined than ever to continue to fight for freedom of the press and for the right of the public to know what is going on in Palestinian society," Daoud Kuttab said upon his release.
